results.title: Robust Federated Learning with Confidence-Weighted Filtering and GAN-Based Completion under Noisy and Incomplete Data
results.content: The proposed approach systematically enhances data integrity through adaptive noise cleaning, collaborative conditional GAN-based synthetic data generation, and robust federated model training. present FEDCNI, a federated learning framework designed to address the joint challenges of label noise and class imbalance in non-IID client data without relying on clean proxy datasets. The method integrates three core components: (1) Knowledge distribution alignment using public datasets to facilitate communication across heterogeneous models without relying on a shared global model; (2) Symmetric loss (SL) to mitigate overfitting to noisy labels by combining cross entropy and reverse cross entropy during local training; and (3) Client Confidence Re-weighting (CCR), a mechanism that quantifies label quality and learning efficiency to reduce the influence of unreliable clients in global aggregation. Our approach integrates adaptive noise cleaning, conditional GAN based synthetic sample generation, and robust federated optimization to improve both data quality and model performance under non-IID conditions.

results.title: How does DeepSeek handle class imbalance during fine-tuning?
results.content: How does DeepSeek handle class imbalance during fine-tuning? Star 35.4KContact UsTry Managed Milvus * How does DeepSeek handle class imbalance during fine-tuning? How does DeepSeek handle class imbalance during fine-tuning? DeepSeek addresses class imbalance during fine-tuning by combining techniques like weighted loss functions, data resampling, and threshold adjustment. These methods ensure the model doesn’t overly favor majority classes while maintaining performance on underrepresented ones. First, DeepSeek uses **weighted loss functions** to adjust the importance of classes during training. For example, in a binary classification task where 95% of samples are negative, the loss for misclassifying a rare positive sample is multiplied by a weight (e.g., 19x for a 1:19 imbalance). This forces the model to prioritize correcting errors on minority classes. In frameworks like PyTorch, this is implemented by passing class weights to the loss function (e.g., `nn.CrossEntropyLoss(weight=class_weights)`). Second, **data resampling** is applied to balance class distributions. For instance, oversampling minority classes by duplicating samples or generating synthetic data using techniques like SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique) helps expose the model to more diverse examples. Conversely, undersampling majority classes reduces redundancy but risks losing valuable data. DeepSeek often combines both: for example, oversampling a rare class (e.g., medical anomalies) while randomly subsampling a frequent class (e.g., normal cases). Additionally, mini-batch sampling strategies ensure each training batch has a balanced mix, preventing the model from biasing toward majority classes within individual gradient updates. After training, DeepSeek may adjust the decision threshold (e.g., lowering it for minority classes) to improve recall. Ensemble methods, such as training multiple models on resampled data subsets and averaging predictions, further stabilize performance. By systematically addressing imbalance at multiple stages, DeepSeek ensures models remain robust and generalize effectively across all classes. #### Recommended Tech Blogs & Tutorials * Introducing Milvus 2.6: Affordable Vector Search at Billion Scale * Introducing the Milvus Sizing Tool: Calculating and Optimizing Your Milvus Deployment Resources * How to Choose the Right Embedding Model? results.title: How to handle noisy labels for robust learning from uncertainty
results.content: How to handle noisy labels for robust learning from uncertainty - ScienceDirect Skip to main contentSkip to article Volume 143, November 2021, Pages 209-217 How to handle noisy labels for robust learning from uncertainty Author links open overlay panel Daehyun Ji a, Dokwan Oh a, Yoonsuk Hyun b, Oh-Min Kwon c, Myeong-Jin Park d Most deep neural networks (DNNs) are trained with large amounts of noisy labels when they are applied. Based on the uncertainty, we propose an efficient learning method called “Uncertain Aware Co-Training (UACT, Algorithm 1)” that robustly trains DNNs even with highly noisy labels given different classification problems. * •We introduce a simple and generic framework for robust learning capable of effectively solving the problem of extremely noisy labels by using different information obtained from the uncertainty, which can also effectively achieve good generalization performance. Similarly to earlier work(Kendall & Gal, 2017), we obtain an uncertainty from somewhat converged network and use the uncertainty as information with which to select clean labels, possibly to help when training with noisy labels. This paper presents new method using both small loss and model uncertainty but effective training techniques called Uncertain Aware Co-Training (UACT), which train DNNs robustly with extreme noisy labels. ### High-frequency covariance estimates with noisy and asynchronous financial data ### Journal of the American Statistical Association (2010) ### Label noise types and their effects on deep learning ### Learning from noisy examples ### Machine Learning (1988) A closer look at memorization in deep networks. * ### Bayesian DivideMix++ for Enhanced Learning with Noisy Labels 2024, Neural Networks Citation Excerpt : An iterative label noise filtering process using ensembles and MC-Dropouts (Köhler, Autenrieth, & Beluch, 2019) was introduced based on the assumption that the predictive uncertainties of clean and noisy data follow two different distributions. Uncertain Aware Co-Training (Ji et al., 2021) studied the relationship between uncertainty and clean labels using MC-Dropouts and used it as a criterion to choose the samples along with the small-loss trick. In this work, we explore the open challenges of neural network memorization and uncertainty in creating robust learning algorithms with noisy labels.
